Former White House press secretary Karoline Leavitt is facing heat on social media for an over-the-top claim about President Donald Trump’s sway over other world leaders.

“I’ve seen him across the table from Xi,” she said on Fox News after Trump’s much-criticized meetings with Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin. “I’ve seen him across the table from Putin. He never leaves these rooms without at least grabbing one deliverable.”

She said Trump “always ends up dominating the conversation” with other world leaders and demands “results on behalf of the American people.”

Trump spent part of this week’s meetings flattering the two strongmen, both of whom have faced allegations of serious human rights abuses. He excitedly called Putin “my friend,” then said the same about Xi.

Trump was effusive afterward as well.

“On a scale of zero to 10, I think it was a 12. It went great,” Trump told NBC News about the meetings. “Fantastic relationships built.”

But outside of “fantastic relationships,” there was no evidence of any “deliverable” mentioned by Leavitt.

If anything, critics said Trump got played by Xi and Putin, who used him as a prop in a photo op while offering nothing solid in return. Instead, the three leaders issued a more general statement saying a nuclear war should never be fought and petroleum production should increase. There was no tangible progress on either issue, and nothing tangible on the wars in Iran and Ukraine, either.
